story: Princess Savitri chose to marry Satyavan, a prince living in the forest, even though she was told he would die within a year. When Yama, the god of death, came for him, she followed Yama, and with each wise answer she won a boon. Finally she asked for children with Satyavan, and Yama had to give her husband's life back.
belief: Married women in North India and Nepal keep the Vat Savitri fast for their husbands' long life, tying threads around a banyan tree.
turns: She chose her husband knowing his fate, against the advice of her father and the sage Narada.
facts: Her story is told to Yudhishthira by the sage Markandeya in the Mahabharata.
Sri Aurobindo wrote 'Savitri', an epic poem of about 24,000 lines, based on her.
Vat Savitri falls on the new moon (or, in some regions, the full moon) of the month of Jyeshtha.
